title: The highest-coefficient conjecture for the polynomials $W_r$
statement:
Let $
u(r)=r(r-1)/2$, let $\epsilon_r=(-1)^{
u(r)}$, and define the coefficients $\gamma(j,r)$ by

$$
\epsilon_r W_r(y)=\sum_{j=0}^{r^2}\gamma(j,r)y^j.
$$

**Highest-coefficient conjecture.** For a given $r>1$, the highest non-zero coefficient is $\gamma(\nu(r+1),r)$, and $\gamma(\nu(r+1),r)>0$. Together with the proved vanishing of the coefficients below degree $
u(r)$, this constrains the degree and sign of the leading term of $W_r$; the source reports no resolution of this conjecture.
references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/1111.1128

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of November 2011).
source_name: John Nuttall, “Determinantal approach to a proof of the Riemann hypothesis”, arXiv:1111.1128 (2011).
